learn.title: Messaging and event-driven architecture
objectives: Tell commands (messages that ask for work) apart from events (notices that something happened) and streams (continuous telemetry), and map each to Service Bus, Event Grid or Event Hubs

Choose between Azure Service Bus and Azure Queue Storage, and pick the right Service Bus tier and features: topics, sessions, duplicate detection, dead-lettering, transactions, private endpoints and geo-replication
Design Event Grid solutions with system, custom, partner and namespace topics, push or pull delivery, filtering, retries, dead-lettering and the MQTT broker
Design Event Hubs ingestion with partitions, partition keys, consumer groups, checkpoints, Capture, the Kafka endpoint and the right tier for retention and event size
Apply competing consumers, publish-subscribe, queue-based load leveling, claim check, outbox, saga, event sourcing and CQRS, and design idempotent consumers for at-least-once delivery
concepts: Command vs event vs stream

A command asks a specific receiver to do work and the sender expects it to be handled (Service Bus). A discrete event announces a state change and the publisher doesn't care who reacts (Event Grid). A stream is a continuous series of telemetry read as a log (Event Hubs).
Service Bus queue vs topic

A queue delivers each message to one consumer (point to point, competing consumers). A topic copies each message to every subscription, and each subscription can filter with SQL or correlation rules. Topics need the Standard or Premium tier; Basic has queues only.
Message sessions

Group related messages by SessionId so one receiver locks the session and processes its messages in FIFO order. Different sessions can still be processed in parallel. Session state can store workflow progress.
Duplicate detection

Service Bus drops a resent message whose MessageId was already seen inside the detection window (default 10 minutes, maximum 7 days). Standard and Premium only. It protects against sender retries, not against consumer reprocessing.
Dead-letter queue

A sub-queue that holds messages that exceeded the maximum delivery count, expired (when dead-lettering on expiration is on) or were dead-lettered by the app. Inspect, fix and resubmit them. Storage queues have no automatic dead-lettering.
Peek-lock vs receive-and-delete
Peek-lock (default) gives at-least-once delivery: the message is locked, then completed or abandoned. Receive-and-delete gives at-most-once: the message is removed as it is read.
Service Bus geo-replication vs Geo-DR

Geo-replication (Premium) replicates metadata and message data to a secondary region, synchronously (RPO 0) or asynchronously with a maximum lag. Geo-Disaster Recovery replicates metadata only. The two can't be combined.
Azure Queue Storage
Simple REST queue inside a storage account: 64 KB messages, huge backlogs up to the account capacity, server-side logs, no ordering guarantee, no topics, no sessions, no duplicate detection.
Event Grid push vs pull

Push delivers events to handlers (webhooks, Functions, queues, Event Hubs) with retries over 24 hours and optional dead-lettering to Blob storage. Pull (namespace topics only) lets the consumer read when it wants and receive through a private endpoint.
Event Grid namespace and MQTT broker
An Event Grid namespace hosts namespace topics (push and pull) and an MQTT broker that supports MQTT v3.1.1 and v5 clients, with routing of MQTT messages to Azure services.
Event Hubs partitions and consumer groups

Partitions are ordered logs that set parallelism; a partition key keeps one device's events in order. Each consumer group is an independent view with its own offsets and checkpoints. Basic allows one consumer group per event hub.
Event Hubs Capture and Kafka

Capture writes the stream to Blob Storage or Data Lake Storage automatically (no code). The Kafka endpoint lets Kafka clients connect by changing configuration only; it needs Standard, Premium or Dedicated.
comparisons: Service Bus for enterprise messaging: FIFO sessions, duplicate detection, dead-lettering, transactions, topics, AMQP. Queue Storage for simple, cheap, very large backlogs (over 80 GB) and server-side transaction logs.
Event Grid routes discrete events to many handlers with filtering and no replay. Event Hubs ingests high-volume streams that consumers read and replay from a retained, partitioned log.
Service Bus for high-value commands that need ordering, transactions and durable pull consumption. Event Grid for lightweight reactive notifications pushed to handlers at low cost per event.

Basic: 1 consumer group, 1-day retention, no Kafka or Capture. Standard: 7-day retention, Kafka, Capture priced separately, Geo-DR. Premium: 90-day retention, Capture included, geo-replication, dynamic partitions. Dedicated: single tenant, events up to 20 MB.
Standard: shared, pay per operation, 256 KB messages. Premium: dedicated messaging units, messages up to 100 MB, private endpoints, customer-managed keys, JMS 2.0 and geo-replication.
Event Grid MQTT broker for standard MQTT pub-sub between any open-source clients. IoT Hub for device management: device twins, direct methods and cloud-to-device messages using device SDKs.
traps: Storage queues are 'usually' FIFO but don't guarantee order; use Service Bus sessions when order matters.
Service Bus Geo-Disaster Recovery doesn't copy messages; only geo-replication protects in-flight data.
Event Grid isn't a log: once an event is delivered or expires it can't be replayed. Use Event Hubs when consumers must re-read data.
Duplicate detection doesn't make processing exactly once; consumers must still be idempotent because delivery is at least once.
Adding more Event Hubs readers than partitions in one consumer group doesn't add throughput; extra readers sit idle.
Service Bus private endpoints and customer-managed keys require the Premium tier.
revision: Command needing guaranteed handling, order or transactions: Service Bus queue.
One message to many filtered subscribers with durable pull: Service Bus topic.
React to Azure resource changes cheaply: Event Grid system topic.
Millions of telemetry events per second with replay: Event Hubs with partition keys.
Kafka clients without code changes: Event Hubs Standard or higher Kafka endpoint.
Payload too big for the broker: claim check (store in Blob, send a reference).
Publish an event reliably after a database write: transactional outbox.
Multi-step business process across services with compensation: saga.

questions.q: A media company queues video-transcoding jobs. The backlog can grow to several hundred gigabytes during peaks, messages are small, order doesn't matter, and the company wants the lowest cost and simplest service. Which messaging service should you recommend?
opts: Azure Queue Storage
Azure Service Bus Standard queues
Azure Service Bus Premium queues
Azure Event Grid custom topics
questions.e: Service Bus queues are limited to 80 GB. Storage queues can hold messages up to the capacity of the storage account at low cost.

questions.q: A wind-farm operator sends millions of sensor readings per second to Azure. Several analytics teams must read the same data independently and replay the last few days when needed. Which service should receive the readings?
opts: Azure Service Bus topics
Azure Queue Storage
Azure Event Hubs
Azure Event Grid custom topics

questions.q: Whenever a customer uploads a file to a storage account, an Azure function must run to scan it. You want no polling and the least custom code. What should you recommend?
opts: Write a message to a Service Bus queue from each uploading client
Subscribe the function to the storage account's Event Grid system topic
Have the function poll the container on a timer every minute
Stream storage diagnostic logs to Event Hubs and filter them

questions.q: An order service publishes order messages. The billing, shipping and loyalty services must each receive their own durable copy and pull it at their own pace. Which Service Bus entity should you recommend?
opts: Three queues that the order service writes to in a loop
A single queue read by all three services
A queue with sessions keyed by service name
A topic with one subscription per service

questions.q: What is the purpose of the dead-letter queue in Azure Service Bus?
opts: It stores a copy of every message for auditing and replay
It buffers messages while the namespace fails over to another region
It holds messages that can't be delivered or processed so they can be inspected and resubmitted
It holds scheduled messages until their delivery time arrives

questions.q: A bank must process account transactions for each account in the exact order they were sent. Which feature should you recommend?
opts: Service Bus message sessions with the account ID as the session ID
Event Grid with advanced filters on the account ID
Azure Queue Storage with a longer visibility timeout
Service Bus duplicate detection with a long window
questions.e: Sessions give FIFO per session ID. Storage queues are usually but not guaranteed to be FIFO.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes an event, as opposed to a command?
opts: It carries a large payload that must be processed inside a transaction
It reports that something already happened, and the publisher doesn't expect a specific receiver to act
It must always be delivered in FIFO order to exactly one consumer
It tells one specific receiver to perform work and expects it to be done

questions.q: In Azure Event Hubs, what does a consumer group provide?
opts: An independent view of the event stream with its own read positions
A way to lock events so that only one reader ever sees them
A filter that delivers only matching events to a subscriber
A set of partitions reserved for a single producer application

questions.q: A start-up needs Service Bus topics with filtered subscriptions for a low-volume app. It doesn't need private endpoints or dedicated capacity and wants to minimise cost. Which tier should you recommend?
opts: Basic
Premium with one messaging unit
Standard
Premium with geo-replication
questions.e: Basic supports queues only. Standard adds topics and subscriptions at a pay-per-operation price.

questions.q: A manufacturer must send commands to individual field devices, track each device's reported configuration and manage device identities at scale using device SDKs. Which service should you recommend?
opts: Azure Service Bus topics
Azure Queue Storage
Azure Event Hubs
Azure IoT Hub

questions.q: A payment API sends a message to a Service Bus queue and retries when it gets a timeout. Sometimes the first send had succeeded, so the same payment is queued twice. You need Service Bus to discard the repeat with minimal code changes. What should you recommend?
opts: Lower the queue's maximum delivery count to 1
Enable duplicate detection and set MessageId to the payment ID
Enable sessions and set SessionId to the payment ID
Switch the receivers to receive-and-delete mode
questions.e: Duplicate detection drops any message whose MessageId was already seen inside the detection window. A business-based MessageId makes the resend predictable.

questions.q: A workflow step reads a message from a Service Bus queue and must send a follow-up message to another queue in the same namespace. Either both must happen or neither. What should you recommend?
opts: Use receive-and-delete mode and send the follow-up afterwards
Use auto-forwarding from the first queue to the second queue
Use a Service Bus transaction that completes the received message and sends via the same entity
Enable duplicate detection on the second queue

questions.q: A logistics company uses Service Bus Premium. If the primary region fails, messages already in the queues must be available in a secondary region, not only the queue definitions. What should you recommend?
opts: Enable Service Bus geo-replication on the namespace
Configure a Service Bus Geo-Disaster Recovery alias
Create a second namespace and recreate entities with a template
Enable zone redundancy in the primary region
questions.e: Geo-Disaster Recovery replicates metadata only. Geo-replication replicates metadata and message data.

questions.q: A trading platform enables Service Bus geo-replication. Regulators require that no acknowledged message is ever lost when the secondary region is promoted, even if publishing latency increases. Which configuration should you recommend?
opts: Geo-Disaster Recovery pairing with planned failover
Asynchronous replication with forced promotion
Synchronous replication
Asynchronous replication with a short maximum lag

questions.q: An insurer on Service Bus Standard needs to send claim documents of about 20 MB to a processing service. It wants to minimise cost and keep the Standard tier. What should you recommend?
opts: Store each document in Blob Storage and send a message that references it
Compress each document and send it in the message body
Enable partitioning on the queue to raise the message size limit
Split each document into many 256 KB messages in one session
questions.e: This is the claim-check pattern: the broker carries a small reference, and the large payload lives in cheap storage.

questions.q: A retailer wants to move existing Apache Kafka producers and consumers to a managed Azure service by changing only connection settings. Volume is moderate and seven days of retention is enough. Which option has the lowest cost that meets the requirement?
opts: Event Hubs Dedicated cluster
Event Hubs Basic tier
Service Bus Premium tier
Event Hubs Standard tier
questions.e: The Kafka endpoint is available in the Standard, Premium and Dedicated tiers of Event Hubs, not in Basic.

questions.q: A telecom company must keep every raw event that arrives in an event hub in Azure Data Lake Storage for later batch analysis. It wants no custom code. What should you recommend?
opts: Route the events to an Event Grid topic with a storage handler
Enable Event Hubs Capture to write the events to Data Lake Storage
Write a consumer that copies each event to Data Lake Storage
Increase the event hub retention to the maximum allowed

questions.q: A team uses an Event Hubs Basic namespace. A second application must now read the same stream independently, with its own checkpoints, without affecting the first. What should you recommend?
opts: Upgrade to the Standard tier and add a second consumer group
Create a second event hub in the same Basic namespace
Add more partitions to the existing event hub
Have both applications share the default consumer group
questions.e: Basic allows only one consumer group per event hub. Standard allows up to 20.

questions.q: An Event Grid subscription pushes events to a webhook that is sometimes offline for more than a day. Events that can't be delivered must be kept for later investigation. What should you configure?
opts: Duplicate detection on the event subscription
Dead-lettering to a Blob Storage container on the event subscription
A longer retention period on the custom topic
A second subscription that delivers to the same webhook
questions.e: Event Grid retries push delivery for up to 24 hours by default, then drops the event unless dead-lettering is configured.

questions.q: A function subscribed to a storage account's Event Grid system topic receives every blob event but only needs blob-created events for .pdf files. You want to reduce invocations and cost. What should you recommend?
opts: Filter the events inside the function code and return early
Route all events to a Service Bus topic with SQL filters
Create a separate storage account just for .pdf files
Add an event type filter and a subject suffix filter to the event subscription

questions.q: A consumer application runs in a locked-down virtual network. It can't expose any public endpoint and must receive events through a private endpoint, reading them when it is ready. Which Event Grid option should you recommend?
opts: A custom topic with a webhook event subscription
A namespace topic with a queue event subscription using pull delivery
A domain topic with push delivery to a webhook
A system topic with push delivery to Azure Functions
questions.e: Pull delivery is available for namespace topics and is the only Event Grid mode that lets consumers receive over a private link.

questions.q: A mobility company has vehicles that use open-source MQTT v5 client libraries to publish to and subscribe on custom hierarchical topics with wildcards. It wants a managed broker in Azure. What should you recommend?
opts: Azure Queue Storage with one queue per vehicle
Azure Event Hubs with the Kafka endpoint
The MQTT broker in an Azure Event Grid namespace
Azure Service Bus Premium topics

questions.q: An image-resizing service can't keep up during sales events. Each image must be resized exactly once by any available worker, and workers should scale out with load. Which pattern should you recommend?
opts: Request-reply with each worker owning a reply queue
Competing consumers reading from a single Service Bus queue
Publish-subscribe with one topic subscription per worker
Event sourcing with workers replaying the full image log

questions.q: A ticketing site sends bookings straight to a database that throttles during sudden spikes, which causes failed requests. Bookings may be processed a few seconds later. Which pattern should you recommend?
opts: Retry each failed request immediately from the web tier
Publish-subscribe with Event Grid in front of the database
Queue-based load leveling with a queue in front of the database writer
Scale the database up permanently to the peak size

questions.q: A Service Bus topic has hundreds of subscriptions, each selecting messages by an exact match on the Region property. Throughput is lower than expected. What should you recommend?
opts: Replace the SQL filters with Boolean true filters
Replace the SQL filters with correlation filters
Move each subscription into its own namespace
Enable duplicate detection on the topic
questions.e: Correlation filters match property values exactly and are evaluated more efficiently than SQL filters.

questions.q: A healthcare company requires that all Service Bus traffic stays on its private network through private endpoints, and that messages are encrypted with its own keys. Which tier should you recommend?
opts: Standard with partitioning enabled
Basic
Standard
Premium

questions.q: Consumers of a clickstream must be able to replay up to 30 days of events directly from Event Hubs. The company wants the lowest-cost multitenant tier that supports this. Which tier should you recommend?
opts: Standard
Basic
Premium
Standard with Capture enabled
questions.e: Maximum retention is 1 day in Basic, 7 days in Standard and 90 days in Premium and Dedicated.

questions.q: An event hub has 16 partitions. Consumers must see each truck's GPS events in the order they were sent, while load is still spread across partitions. What should you recommend?
opts: Send each event with the truck ID as the partition key
Send all events to partition 0 by specifying its ID
Let the service assign partitions in round-robin order
Use a separate consumer group for each truck

questions.q: A team says: 'Our Event Grid and Service Bus consumers don't need to handle duplicates because both services deliver each message exactly once.' Is this correct?
opts: Only Event Grid is exactly once; Service Bus is at least once
Only Service Bus is exactly once; Event Grid is at least once
No. Both deliver at least once, so consumers should be idempotent
Yes. Both guarantee exactly-once delivery by default

questions.q: A worker reads from an Azure Queue Storage queue. A malformed message keeps reappearing and crashing the worker. You must stop this without changing services. What should you recommend?
opts: Check the dequeue count and move messages over a threshold to a separate poison queue
Enable automatic dead-lettering on the storage queue
Set the message time-to-live to infinite
Enable duplicate detection on the storage queue
questions.e: Storage queues have no automatic dead-lettering. The app (or the Functions queue trigger) uses the dequeue count to move poison messages.

questions.q: Each of 300 store systems writes to its own Service Bus queue for isolation. A central service must consume all of them from one place. What should you recommend with the least code?
opts: Copy messages with a scheduled function that reads every queue
Configure auto-forwarding from each store queue to a central queue
Have the central service open 300 receivers in a loop
Replace the store queues with one Event Grid custom topic

questions.q: A subscription service must send a renewal reminder message for processing exactly 14 days after sign-up. You want Service Bus to hold it until then without a timer service. What should you recommend?
opts: Use a session that is locked for 14 days
Set the message time-to-live to 14 days
Send the message and defer it until the reminder date
Send a scheduled message with the enqueue time set to 14 days later

questions.q: A custom inventory application wants to announce 'stock low' events to several handlers with filtering, using push delivery over HTTP. Which Event Grid resource should the application publish to?
opts: A custom topic
An event hub
A system topic
A partner topic

questions.q: A SaaS provider publishes events for thousands of customers. Each customer may subscribe only to its own events, and the provider wants one endpoint to publish to and central management. What should you recommend?
opts: One event hub with one partition per customer
One Service Bus namespace per customer
One Event Grid custom topic per customer in separate subscriptions
An Event Grid domain with one domain topic per customer

questions.q: Consider these statements. 1: Azure Queue Storage keeps server-side logs of all transactions on the queue. 2: Azure Queue Storage supports automatic duplicate detection. 3: Service Bus queues support AMQP 1.0. 4: Service Bus queues can grow larger than storage queues. Which statements are true?
opts: Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
Statements 2 and 4 only

questions.q: An e-commerce firm needs order messages per customer processed in order, sender retries discarded automatically, failed messages kept for review, traffic only over private endpoints and predictable performance isolated from other tenants. What should you recommend?
opts: Service Bus Premium queue with sessions, duplicate detection and dead-lettering
Azure Queue Storage with a private endpoint and a poison queue
Event Grid namespace topic with pull delivery and a private endpoint
Service Bus Standard queue with sessions, duplicate detection and dead-lettering

questions.q: Workers read from an Azure Queue Storage queue. Sometimes an order's 'cancel' message is processed before its 'create' message, and after worker crashes some messages are processed twice. Which change best fixes both problems?
opts: Use one worker only and enable infinite time-to-live
Move to an Event Grid custom topic with retries
Move to Service Bus sessions keyed by order ID and make handlers idempotent
Increase the visibility timeout and add more workers
questions.e: Storage queues don't guarantee order, and a crashed worker's message reappears after the visibility timeout. Sessions give per-order FIFO; idempotency handles redelivery.

questions.q: A team plans Service Bus Premium geo-replication for disaster recovery and also wants to send 40 MB messages using Premium large-message support. What should you recommend?
opts: Keep messages small with the claim-check pattern, because geo-replication doesn't support large messages
Enable partitioning so large messages replicate in pieces
Use asynchronous replication, which supports large messages
Combine geo-replication with Geo-Disaster Recovery for large messages

questions.q: A fleet-analytics platform must ingest millions of events per second, keep them for several days and let new consumers replay past data from any point. Which service should you NOT recommend as the ingestion layer?
opts: Azure Event Hubs Standard with Kafka clients
Azure Event Hubs Dedicated
Azure Event Hubs Premium
Azure Event Grid custom topics
questions.e: Event Grid delivers discrete events and keeps nothing for replay after delivery.

questions.q: An order service saves an order to Azure SQL Database and then publishes an 'order created' event to Service Bus. If the service crashes between the two steps, the event is lost. You can't use distributed transactions. What should you recommend?
opts: Use Service Bus transactions that include the SQL write
Publish the event first and then save the order to the database
Write the event to an outbox table in the same database transaction and relay it to Service Bus
Enable duplicate detection on the Service Bus topic

questions.q: A lending platform must keep a full, immutable history of every change to each loan, rebuild a loan's state at any past date and feed separate read-optimised views. Which approach should you recommend?
opts: Publish-subscribe with Event Grid and no stored events
CRUD tables with nightly backups of each table
Queue-based load leveling with a Storage queue
Event sourcing with CQRS projections for the read views

questions.q: Millions of files land in a storage account each day. Each file must trigger processing, but the processor has limited capacity, must pull work at its own pace and must not lose work if it is down for hours. What should you recommend?
opts: An Event Grid system topic that delivers blob-created events to a Service Bus queue
An Event Grid system topic that pushes events straight to the processor's webhook
A timer job that lists the container for new blobs every minute
An event hub with Capture enabled pointing at the same container

questions.q: A partitioned Service Bus queue has duplicate detection enabled. Producers resend messages with the same MessageId but sometimes a different partition key, and duplicates still get through. What explains this?
opts: The detection window applies only to scheduled messages
With partitioning, uniqueness is based on MessageId plus partition key
Duplicate detection compares the full message body, not MessageId
Duplicate detection isn't supported on partitioned entities

questions.q: A gaming company expects telemetry to grow tenfold over two years and wants to add partitions to an existing event hub later without recreating it. Which tier should you recommend?
opts: Premium
Standard with auto-inflate
Basic
Standard
questions.e: Dynamic partition scale-out is available in Premium and Dedicated. In Standard, plan the partition count at creation.

questions.q: An event hub has 8 partitions. A team scales its consumer from 8 to 24 instances in the same consumer group, but throughput doesn't improve. What is the most likely reason?
opts: Consumer groups limit throughput to one instance per namespace
Checkpointing stops working when more than 8 readers run
Each partition is owned by one reader in the group, so the extra instances are idle
Readers must use the Kafka endpoint to scale beyond 8

questions.q: A travel site books a flight, a hotel and a car through three separate services, each with its own database. If the car booking fails, the earlier bookings must be undone. Which pattern should you recommend?
opts: A saga with compensating actions coordinated by messages
A two-phase commit across the three databases
Competing consumers on a single shared queue
Event Hubs Capture of all booking events

questions.q: Messages for each insurance claim arrive in sequence. A worker that crashes mid-claim must let another worker resume from the last completed step without an external database. What should you recommend?
opts: Storage queues with progress written into message metadata
Service Bus deferral with a fixed lock duration
Service Bus sessions with session state updated in a transaction with message completion
Event Hubs checkpoints written by each worker

questions.q: Consider these Event Hubs statements. 1: Capture is available in the Basic tier. 2: The Kafka endpoint is available in the Standard tier. 3: Geo-replication is available in the Premium tier. 4: Basic supports up to 20 consumer groups. Which statements are true?
opts: Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1 and 2 only

questions.q: An Event Grid push subscription to an on-premises webhook loses events whenever the site's internet link is down for two days. The consumer team wants to fetch events when the link returns, without data loss up to the retention limit. What should you recommend?
opts: Increase the maximum delivery attempts on the push subscription
Enable duplicate detection on the custom topic
Add a second push subscription to the same webhook
Move to an Event Grid namespace topic with pull delivery

questions.q: Gold-tier customer requests must be processed faster than standard requests, even under heavy load. Both types arrive from one publisher. What should you recommend?
opts: A Service Bus topic with filtered subscriptions per priority and more consumers on the gold one
A single Storage queue with a shorter visibility timeout for gold
A single queue with a priority property that consumers sort locally
Scheduled messages that delay all standard requests
questions.e: This is the priority queue pattern: separate channels let you scale consumers per priority.

questions.q: Which Azure service stores events in a partitioned, retained log that consumers read by offset and can re-read from an earlier position?
opts: Azure Service Bus queues
Azure Event Hubs
Azure Queue Storage
Azure Event Grid

questions.q: Which Service Bus receive mode gives at-most-once delivery?
opts: Receive-and-delete
Peek-lock
Peek-lock with automatic lock renewal
Peek-lock with sessions enabled
questions.e: Receive-and-delete removes the message as it is read, so a crash loses it. Peek-lock gives at-least-once delivery.

questions.q: What best describes the publish-subscribe pattern?
opts: Many workers compete so each message is processed by one of them
A sender waits on a reply queue for a response to each request
A sender publishes once and every interested subscriber gets its own copy
A queue absorbs spikes so a backend processes at a steady rate

questions.q: Which open standard event schema does Azure Event Grid support for interoperability across platforms?
opts: Apache Avro 1.11
CloudEvents 1.0
OpenAPI 3.0
AsyncAPI 2.0

questions.q: An integration team needs a queue that clients can use over the AMQP 1.0 standard protocol. Which service should you recommend?
opts: Azure Queue Storage
Azure Event Grid custom topics
Azure Blob Storage
Azure Service Bus

questions.q: Operations wants an automation runbook to start whenever a virtual machine in a subscription is deallocated. Which service should deliver the notification?
opts: Azure Queue Storage
Azure Event Hubs
Azure Event Grid
Azure Service Bus Premium

questions.q: Where can Azure Event Hubs Capture write captured event data?
opts: Azure Blob Storage or Azure Data Lake Storage
Azure SQL Database or Azure Cosmos DB
Azure Managed Redis or Azure Table Storage
Azure Files or Azure NetApp Files

questions.q: An Event Hubs Standard namespace is sometimes throttled when traffic rises. You want capacity to grow automatically with minimal administration. What should you recommend?
opts: Increase the event retention period
Enable auto-inflate for throughput units
Add consumer groups to the event hub
Enable Capture to Blob Storage

questions.q: A company wants to react in Azure to events raised by a supported third-party SaaS provider, without building its own polling integration. Which Event Grid resource should it use?
opts: A system topic
A custom topic
A domain topic
A partner topic

questions.q: A colleague says: 'Azure Queue Storage guarantees first-in-first-out delivery.' Is this correct?
opts: No. Messages are usually FIFO, but order isn't guaranteed
Yes, but only when messages are Base64 encoded
No. Storage queues always deliver in random order
Yes. FIFO is guaranteed for every storage queue

questions.q: A consumer receives a 'ship order' message before the matching 'payment confirmed' message. It must set the ship message aside and process it later, retrieving it directly when payment is confirmed. What should you recommend?
opts: Schedule a copy of the message for one hour later
Dead-letter the message and resubmit it later
Defer the message and later receive it by its sequence number
Abandon the message so it returns to the queue

questions.q: A Service Bus consumer takes several minutes per message. Messages are often processed twice and some end up in the dead-letter queue, even though processing succeeds. What should you recommend first?
opts: Switch the queue to receive-and-delete mode
Increase the duplicate detection window
Lower the queue's maximum delivery count
Enable automatic lock renewal in the receiver for the processing time
questions.e: When the lock expires before completion, the message becomes available again and its delivery count grows until it is dead-lettered.

questions.q: Price-update messages are useless after an hour and have a time-to-live set. Auditors want to see which updates expired without being processed. What should you configure?
opts: Enable duplicate detection with a one-hour window
Enable dead-lettering on message expiration for the queue
Turn off time-to-live and delete old messages manually
Use auto-delete on idle for the queue

questions.q: An event hub feeds billing. After a regional outage, events not yet consumed must be readable in another region. The current namespace uses Standard with Geo-Disaster Recovery. What should you recommend?
opts: Move to Premium and enable Event Hubs geo-replication
Keep Standard and fail over the Geo-Disaster Recovery alias
Add more partitions to spread events across regions
Enable Capture in Standard to write events to a local container
questions.e: Geo-Disaster Recovery replicates metadata only. Geo-replication, in Premium and Dedicated, also replicates event data.

questions.q: A payments platform on Service Bus Standard sees variable latency at busy times because resources are shared with other tenants. It needs predictable performance and the ability to scale capacity. What should you recommend?
opts: Service Bus Basic with more namespaces
Service Bus Standard with partitioned queues
Azure Queue Storage with a premium storage account
Service Bus Premium with messaging units sized for the load

questions.q: A company is moving Java applications from an on-premises ActiveMQ broker to Azure and wants to keep using the JMS 2.0 API with few code changes. What should you recommend?
opts: Azure Queue Storage
Azure Service Bus Premium
Azure Event Grid namespace

opts: Event Grid system topics that push to the SIEM's webhook
A Service Bus queue that the SIEM polls over AMQP
Event Grid system topics that deliver to an event hub read by the SIEM
A storage queue per subscription read by the SIEM

questions.q: You create an Event Grid subscription to a new custom webhook, but the subscription fails to activate and no events arrive. What is the most likely cause?
opts: The endpoint didn't complete the subscription validation handshake
The topic has no dead-letter destination configured

Duplicate detection rejected the first event

questions.q: An Event Grid system topic must deliver events to a Service Bus queue that has local (SAS) authentication disabled. You want no secrets to manage. What should you recommend?
opts: Create a user account for Event Grid in the namespace

Enable a managed identity on the topic and grant it the Service Bus Data Sender role

questions.q: You add a new subscription to a Service Bus topic and don't define any filter. Which messages does it receive?
opts: Only messages that have a session ID
All messages sent to the topic after it was created
No messages until a filter is added
All messages ever sent to the topic, including earlier ones

questions.q: A worker reads Azure Queue Storage messages and some jobs run longer than expected. Other workers must not pick up a message while it is still being processed. What should you recommend?
opts: Enable sessions on the storage queue
Delete the message before starting the job
Extend the message's visibility timeout while the job runs
Set the message time-to-live to a longer value

questions.q: A small app already uses Azure Queue Storage and must hand off scanned forms of up to 5 MB to a worker. It wants to minimise cost and keep its current service. What should you recommend?
opts: Upload each form to Blob Storage and queue a message with the blob URL
Split each form across several queue messages
Move to Service Bus Premium for large messages
Base64 encode each form into the queue message

questions.q: An Event Hubs consumer must resume from where it stopped after a restart, without reprocessing the whole retention period. What should you recommend?
opts: Create a new consumer group on every restart
Use receive-and-delete mode on the event hub
Use the event processor client with checkpoints in Blob Storage
Enable duplicate detection on the event hub

questions.q: A pricing event hub carries updates keyed by product ID. New consumers only need the latest price for each product, not the full history. Which Event Hubs feature should you recommend?
opts: Capture to Data Lake Storage
Log compaction on the event hub
An additional consumer group
Auto-inflate of throughput units

questions.q: Factory machines publish MQTT messages to an Event Grid namespace. The data must be sent on to a high-volume analytics stream in Azure without custom relay code. What should you recommend?
opts: Have each machine also publish to Event Hubs over Kafka
Configure Event Hubs Capture on the Event Grid namespace
Run a VM that subscribes to all topics and forwards data
Route MQTT messages to a namespace topic with an event subscription to Event Hubs

questions.q: A bank's transfer instructions must be processed in order per account, inside transactions, and kept until a consumer explicitly completes them. Which service should you recommend over Event Grid?
opts: Azure Service Bus
Azure Event Hubs Basic
Azure Queue Storage
Azure Event Grid domains

questions.q: Thousands of customers each send ordered message streams. Order matters only within a customer, and the company wants many workers processing different customers in parallel. What should you recommend?
opts: One Service Bus namespace per customer
Duplicate detection keyed by customer ID
One queue and a single worker to keep global order
Sessions keyed by customer ID, with workers accepting different sessions

questions.q: Four microservices react to each other's events with no central controller. The team now struggles to see the state of each business process. Which change addresses this?
opts: Replace the events with direct synchronous HTTP calls everywhere
Add more topic subscriptions so every service sees every event
Introduce an orchestrator that coordinates the steps and tracks process state
Increase the retention of the events in Event Hubs
questions.e: Choreography keeps services loosely coupled but spreads process logic. An orchestrator centralises flow and status at the cost of a coordinator.

questions.q: A front end sends a quote request through Service Bus and must receive the matching reply on a shared reply queue, even when many front-end instances are running. What should you recommend?
opts: Poll the request queue until the original message disappears
Use Event Grid to push the reply to every instance
Have every instance read the shared reply queue and discard others' replies
Set ReplyToSessionId and have each instance accept its own session on the reply queue

questions.q: A developer assumes Event Grid always delivers events to a handler in the order they were published. Is this correct?
opts: No. Order isn't guaranteed, so handlers must tolerate out-of-order events
Yes. Event Grid delivers events in strict FIFO order
Yes, but only for events from system topics
No, but enabling dead-lettering makes delivery ordered

questions.q: Producer apps must only send to a Service Bus queue, and consumer apps must only receive from it. You want to use Microsoft Entra ID without shared keys. What should you recommend?
opts: Assign the Contributor role on the namespace to all apps
Give all apps the Azure Service Bus Data Owner role
Assign Azure Service Bus Data Sender and Data Receiver roles to the apps' managed identities
Create one SAS policy with Send and Listen for all apps

questions.q: A genomics firm must publish individual events of up to 10 MB directly to Event Hubs, without splitting them or using external storage. Which tier should you recommend?
opts: Basic
Dedicated
Premium
Standard
questions.e: Maximum publication size is 1 MB in Standard and Premium and 20 MB in Dedicated.

questions.q: Many teams produce and consume Avro events on Event Hubs, and schema changes keep breaking consumers. You want central schema governance with minimal extra infrastructure. What should you recommend?
opts: A shared Avro file in a Git repository
Event Hubs Capture to Data Lake Storage
Event Grid advanced filters on the event type
Azure Schema Registry in the Event Hubs namespace

questions.q: Each test environment creates its own topic subscription that should disappear automatically when the environment stops using it. What should you recommend?
opts: Set a short message time-to-live on the topic
Set auto-delete on idle for the subscriptions
Lower the maximum delivery count to 1
Enable dead-lettering on filter evaluation errors

questions.q: A team plans to use Event Hubs as a job queue where each job is handled by one worker, failed jobs are retried individually and jobs that keep failing are set aside automatically. What should you recommend instead?
opts: An event hub with Capture to Blob Storage
An event hub with one consumer group per worker
A Service Bus queue with peek-lock and dead-lettering
An Event Grid custom topic with webhook handlers
questions.e: Event Hubs tracks a read offset per partition, not per-message completion. Competing consumers, per-message retries and dead-lettering are Service Bus features.

questions.q: A consumer pulls events from an Event Grid namespace topic. When a downstream database is unavailable, it must hand an event back for later delivery instead of losing it, and permanently failing events must be kept for review. What should you recommend?
opts: Release the event back to the subscription and configure dead-lettering for failures
Switch the subscription to push delivery to a webhook with no retries
Acknowledge the event and store it in local memory until the database recovers
Reject every event so that the publisher resends it later
questions.e: With pull delivery, the consumer acknowledges, releases or rejects each event, giving it full control over consumption.

questions.q: Consider these Event Grid statements. 1: Pull delivery is available for namespace topics. 2: Push delivery retries for up to 24 hours by default. 3: Pull delivery lets consumers receive events over a private link. 4: System topics support pull delivery. Which statements are true?
opts: Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
Statements 1 and 2 only

questions.q: A smart-building vendor needs devices from many manufacturers to use any open-source MQTT v5 client, publish to custom topic hierarchies, receive retained last-known values and talk device-to-device. Which service should you recommend?
opts: Event Hubs Premium with the Kafka endpoint
Service Bus Premium topics over AMQP
Azure IoT Hub with device twins
Event Grid namespace MQTT broker
questions.e: IoT Hub uses fixed device-to-cloud topics and isn't a general MQTT pub-sub broker. Event Grid's broker supports custom topics, wildcards, retain and one-to-many messaging.

questions.q: A team implements event sourcing and uses Event Hubs Premium as the only permanent store of all domain events, relying on retention to rebuild state years later. What is the flaw?
opts: Event Hubs Premium doesn't support the Kafka endpoint
Event Hubs retention is time-limited, so it can't be the permanent event store
Event Hubs doesn't allow more than one consumer group
Event Hubs can't preserve order within a partition

questions.q: After adopting CQRS, users sometimes save a change and then don't see it on the next page, which reads from a separate read model updated through events. What explains this?
opts: The read model is eventually consistent with the write model
The read and write models must share the same database
The event broker delivered the event to the wrong subscriber
The command model rejected the write without an error

questions.q: After a Service Bus Geo-Disaster Recovery failover, the queues exist in the secondary namespace but contain none of the messages that were waiting in the primary. What explains this, and what should you recommend?
opts: Messages expired during failover; raise the queue time-to-live
Duplicate detection dropped them; disable it before failing over
The failover was planned; a forced failover would have copied messages
Geo-DR replicates only metadata; use geo-replication to replicate message data

questions.q: A platform raises about 2 million small 'profile updated' notifications a month. Three services each react to a filtered subset by HTTP. No ordering, transactions or replay are needed. Which option is most cost-effective?
opts: Service Bus Premium topic with three subscriptions
Event Grid custom topic with filtered push subscriptions
Event Hubs Premium with three consumer groups
Event Hubs Dedicated cluster with Capture

questions.q: A claims worker must, for each message, update session state, complete the message and send a result message to another queue in the same namespace, all as one unit so a crash leaves nothing half-done. What should you recommend?
opts: Event Grid with dead-lettering to Blob Storage
Storage queues with progress stored in message content
Event Hubs checkpoints taken after each send
Service Bus sessions with all three operations in one transaction using send-via

questions.q: A Service Bus namespace uses asynchronous geo-replication. After a forced promotion during an outage, consumers see some messages they had already completed. What should you recommend?
opts: Switch to Geo-Disaster Recovery, which prevents duplicates
Lower the duplicate detection window to 20 seconds
Make consumers idempotent, as forced promotion can lose or duplicate state changes
Use receive-and-delete mode so completions replicate first

questions.q: A retailer has three flows: payment commands that must not be lost, store sensor telemetry at very high volume with replay, and notifications when blobs are created. Which mapping should you recommend?
opts: Event Hubs, Service Bus queue, Event Grid system topic
Storage queue, Event Grid custom topic, Service Bus topic
Event Grid custom topic, Service Bus topic, Event Hubs
Service Bus queue, Event Hubs, Event Grid system topic

questions.q: Flash-sale alerts pushed by Event Grid are worthless after 10 minutes. If the handler is down, Event Grid keeps retrying for hours and delivers stale alerts. What should you recommend?
opts: Raise the maximum delivery attempts on the subscription
Set the event subscription's event time-to-live to 10 minutes
Add an advanced filter on the event time
Enable dead-lettering without changing the retry policy

questions.q: An on-premises app must receive commands from Azure. The firewall allows no inbound connections and only outbound HTTPS on port 443. Which design should you recommend?
opts: Have Event Grid push commands to a webhook on the app
Open an inbound port so Azure can call the app directly
Have the app consume from Event Hubs over Kafka on port 9093
Have the app receive from a Service Bus queue using AMQP over WebSockets

questions.q: Partners upload large CAD files that a processing service must handle. You want no large payloads in the broker, no extra code in partner clients and automatic notification when each file arrives. What should you recommend?
opts: Partners send each file to a Service Bus Premium queue
Partners upload to Blob Storage, and blob-created events from Event Grid tell the processor
Partners stream each file to Event Hubs in 1 MB chunks
Partners publish each file as an event to an Event Grid custom topic

questions.q: An Azure Functions app with a Service Bus trigger scales out and processes a customer's messages out of order, even though senders set SessionId. What should you recommend?
opts: Enable duplicate detection on the queue
Switch the trigger to receive-and-delete mode
Disable scale-out so a single instance reads the queue
Enable sessions on the queue and turn on session handling in the trigger
questions.e: SessionId only gives FIFO when the entity requires sessions and the receiver accepts sessions.

questions.q: Consider these Service Bus statements. 1: Basic supports topics. 2: Basic supports duplicate detection. 3: Premium supports private endpoints. 4: Premium supports geo-replication. Which statements are true?
opts: Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 3 and 4 only
Statements 1 and 3 only
